meta.title: Calendar
meta.description: A multi-view scheduling system. Month, week, day, and agenda views with overlap layout, drag-to-create, drag-to-reschedule, a mini navigator, and a floating event popover — bring your own event data and render logic.

blocks.content: Most calendar libraries own your data model. You adapt your tasks, appointments, or posts to fit their event shape. Their event card is what you get. You style around it. When you need something the library didn't anticipate, you file an issue and wait.

This system owns nothing but the hard parts. The overlap layout algorithm that places simultaneous events side by side. The sweep-line collision detection that computes which events share a time column. The drag interactions — click-drag to create, drag to move, edge-drag to resize — all writing directly to the DOM with zero React re-renders during the gesture. The @floating-ui event popover that never escapes the viewport. Your event shape, your render logic, your handlers. The system just does the layout.

children.name: calendar-engine.ts
children.comment: overlap algorithm, date utils — no React

blocks.title: The overlap algorithm
blocks.content: calendar-engine.ts contains computeOverlapLayout() — a sweep-line algorithm that groups overlapping events into collision sets, then greedily assigns each event to the first column where it doesn't overlap the previous event. The result is the column index and total column count for each event, which the time grid uses to compute left% and width%. It runs once when events change and is memoized per day column.
All four views, a mini navigator, and a custom event popover. Click any event to open its popover. Click-drag on an empty slot to select a time range. Switch views with the tabs in the top right.
Calendar uses @floating-ui/react for the event popover. Install it if you haven't already.

steps.title: Import and use
steps.code:
import {
  CalendarRoot,
  CalendarNav,
  CalendarMonthView,
  CalendarEventPopover,
  type CalendarEventBase,
} from "@/components/bevelui/calendar"

blocks.content: Wrap your layout in CalendarRoot, pass your events, then compose the views you need as children. CalendarRoot provides context — every child component reads from it via useCalendar().

blocks.title: Inner component pattern
blocks.content: Any component that needs useCalendar() must be a child of CalendarRoot. The Shell pattern — a component that composes the views and reads activeView to decide which to render — is the standard approach.
CalendarEventBase is the minimum contract the system needs. Extend it with whatever fields your domain requires — the generic T flows through every component and hook.
Every visual surface in every view is a render prop. If you don't pass one, a sensible default renders. Pass one to take full control.

blocks.title: renderEvent receives the view name
blocks.content: The second argument to renderEvent is the current view ("month" | "week" | "day" | "agenda"). Use it to render a compact version in month view and a detailed version in week/day view — the same function, different output.
The same system covers very different products. Here are three patterns.

blocks.title: Positioned by @floating-ui
blocks.content: CalendarEventPopover uses useFloating with flip and shift middleware — it automatically moves to whichever side has room and never escapes the viewport. It anchors to the DOM element that was clicked, via the selectedEventAnchor stored in context.
